label: "c" just after a b-initial prefix, early in the input (t=3-4)
explanation: Sparse feature that fires almost only in the original phase at steps 3-5 (97% of mass; never in the copy phase, never at t<3 or t>6). It is driven by the conjunction of a sequence starting with b (89% of mass) and the previous input being c (74% of mass), i.e. the step right after prefixes like b ? c or b ? ? c. The strongest activations happen when the current input is also b (e.g. b e s c [b]), and prev2 = s/c/t/e makes it more likely. The predicate (first=b, prev=c, t in 3-4) gets about 38% precision and 51% recall on dev: plenty of b..c contexts stay silent, and weaker activations show up in contexts like ? ? c b or b-initial prefixes without c. So the direction is clear but the exact gating is not captured.
